glossary_propose_entity_edit.note: PROVEN LIVE, and the PILOT OVERTURNED MY OWN PLAN before a line was written. The 101 calls / 12 sessions / 0 ok are a JULY record: 92 of 101 sent a placeholder into a UUID field (68x entity_id='placeholder_id_1', 24x book_id='current_book_id_placeholder'), and in ALL 8 of those sessions the model never called a read that yields an entity id. I was about to bind entity_id to EntityRef and rewire CP-5.3 into the frontend path, and a real finding does sit behind that: validate_frontend_tool_args runs ~150 lines BEFORE identifier resolution, so the resolver is structurally unreachable for frontend tools, and this is the one entity_id field of 19 that is not bound. THE PILOT SAID DON'T BUILD IT. Driven today on the agui surface the model does it correctly: glossary_search -> glossary_get_entity -> propose with a REAL entity_id, attr_value_id and base_version. The tool is not broken. THE ACTUAL DEFECT, which only the pilot could have found: it could never be RECORDED as succeeding. A frontend tool SUSPENDS; ok:true is written only where a dispatch returns; and the human's decision arrived on the resume as prose in the model's context and nothing measurable. The row said deferred forever, so 'the user applied the edit' and 'the user walked away' were the same row. FIX: instrument.resolve_deferred types the resolution (applied_saved -> done, dismissed -> refused/dismissed_by_user, applied_conflict -> retryable_modified, anything unknown -> failed and never guessed into a success), and the resume persists it. NOT FIXED, recorded as DQ-4: a resumed turn OVERWRITES its own first pass's tool_calls -- watched sequence_num 2 go from 3 rows to 1 -- which erases the deferred row of every suspension a human returned to and makes the size of the loss unmeasurable rather than merely large. NOT FIXED, recorded as DQ-5: the resolver's unreachability plus this tool's missing EntityRef binding; its corpus contains ZERO names, so CP-5 section 7 says a member with no subject is not written.
